To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the impact of population aging on self-perceptions of aging is not uniform across regions, and (2) the regional differences are explained by the different regional patterns of population aging.
(1) older adults’ perceptions of aging are more positive in areas with higher proportions of older adults and (2) this association is stronger for women and those with lower levels of education.

(a) the regional impact of population ageing on individual self-perceptions of ageing was not uniform, but rather varied across regions; (b) this regional impact was stronger in areas with a high proportion of elderly residents; (c) in areas with a low proportion of elderly residents, population ageing was associated with an improvement in self-perceptions of aging.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the regional impact of population aging has an effect on the self-perceptions of aging in Germany, which can be measured on the basis of the German Ageing Study (DEAS).
the question of how the regional context of aging affects individual self-perceptions.
the impact of population aging on individual self-perceptions of aging.
